clue.text: Une préparation à base d'herbes — ou un pansement?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a preparation made with herbs, a herby salad sauce such as vinaigrette
second meaning: pansement is the word a Parisian uses for a bandage on a wound

explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is in French, which is itself the joke: the second reading is simply 'a dressing' said in French.
explanation.definitionFit: Vinaigrette flavoured with herbs is the classic salad sauce, and a bandage named in French is a dressing of that nationality.

clue.text: Metres short, summit in sight — and no way round mountains

indicators.note: Metres is cut short to its opening letter, its standard abbreviation

parts.note: the unit whose abbreviation is used

indicators.note: the retort goes round the letter from sight, holding it within

parts.note: the scoffing retort 'As if!' means no way

indicators.note: the summit of a down word is its top, so only the first letter of sight is used

parts.note: the word whose top letter is taken

explanation.surface: A climber a few metres from the top glimpses the summit, with no route around the peaks.
explanation.definitionFit: A massif is a compact group of mountains forming a single mass, such as the Massif Central in France.

clue.text: People for whom figures are important must take after me!

definitions.text: People for whom figures are important
definitions.meaning: reads like accountants or dieters, but figures here are numbers in a sum
sounds like 'imitate me', but take means subtract: what follows this symbol is taken away

explanation.walkthrough: 'Take after' looks like resembling a parent; in arithmetic the number after the symbol is taken away from the one before.
explanation.definitionFit: The minus symbol in arithmetic tells anyone working with numbers to deduct what follows it.

clue.text: Notices put up about show

indicators.note: the reversed word for put goes about the word for show, around it
in a down clue, up means the word for put is read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: to put something down is to set it
to show someone the way is to lead

explanation.surface: Posters about a show are pinned up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put up' looks like one phrase meaning displayed; split it, put gives the word and up turns it over.
explanation.definitionFit: Tele-ads are television commercials, adverts broadcast as notices to viewers.

clue.text: Enter beginner in Witchery Skills in Wizardry papers: travel up in this

definitions.text: Enter beginner in Witchery Skills in Wizardry papers: travel up in this

indicators.note: the reversed word for travel is put in the whole construction
the first letter and skills enter the word for wizardry, going inside it
the letters are placed in the word for wizardry, within it

parts.note: a hex is a spell, an act of wizardry

indicators.note: the beginner in a word is its opening letter

parts.note: the word whose first letter is used
arts are skills
the press means the newspapers

indicators.note: in a down answer, up means reading the travel word backwards

parts.note: to go is to travel

explanation.surface: A new pupil enrols at a school of witchcraft and wizardry, papers in hand, and rides up on this.
explanation.walkthrough: Hogwarts in the Harry Potter books is a School of Witchcraft and Wizardry; its train takes pupils, newcomers included, up to school from London, so the whole clue also defines it.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Harry Potter stories the school train leaves King's Cross from Platform Nine and Three-Quarters carrying pupils north to the castle.

clue.text: Sound disapproving: clueless (but apologetic) trumpeter has arrived

indicators.note: the trumpeter has the letters for arrived, holding them inside his name

parts.note: Humphrey Lyttelton, known as Humph, a jazz trumpeter who chaired the BBC radio comedy I'm Sorry I Haven't a Clue
ARR is the timetable abbreviation for arrives or arrived

explanation.surface: A trumpeter turns up late and someone grumbles disapprovingly.
explanation.walkthrough: I'm Sorry I Haven't a Clue is a long-running BBC radio panel game: hence clueless but apologetic.
explanation.definitionFit: To make a gruff throat-clearing noise to signal displeasure is the verb sense of the word.

clue.text: Ex-landlord takes exam in Religious Correspondence

indicators.note: the former landlord takes the exam inside himself, so it sits within his letters

parts.note: ex- means former, which is past
a landlord is one who lets property, a letter
an oral is a spoken examination

explanation.surface: A retired landlord sits an exam in a correspondence course on religion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Landlord' is read whimsically as someone who lets.
explanation.definitionFit: A bishop's pastoral letter is an official message to the clergy or faithful of a diocese, read out in churches.

clue.text: Right age to succeed a keeper

indicators.note: succeeding means coming after, so these pieces follow the a

parts.note: taken as written
to age is to mature

explanation.surface: The right age to take over as a goalkeeper or wicketkeeper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keeper' suggests sport, but it is the iron bar laid across a magnet's poles.
explanation.definitionFit: The soft iron bar placed across the poles of a horseshoe magnet to preserve its strength is called both its keeper and its armature.

clue.text: Valley supplying wine or cases of comparable quality

indicators.note: the two letters of or encase the valley, one on each side

parts.note: taken as written
the Napa Valley in California is famous for its wine

explanation.surface: A wine valley sends out bottles or cases of similar quality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cases' looks like crates of wine but tells the word or to enclose the valley.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that are on a par are equal in standard, from the idea of being level at par value.

clue.text: Turn set on

indicators.note: turn tells us to turn the word for set round, back to front

parts.note: jelly sets, or gels

explanation.surface: An instruction to turn a machine set to on.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the on side and leg side are the same half of the field, so 'on' is a fair definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricket names the half of the field behind the batter's legs the on side or leg side interchangeably.

clue.text: Admitting I make puzzles, bet and drink

indicators.note: the bet admits the setter's phrase, letting it inside

parts.note: an ante is a stake put up in poker
taken as written
a crossword compiler sets puzzles

explanation.surface: A setter confesses to compiling puzzles, gambling and drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I make puzzles' is the setter speaking of themself: I SET.
explanation.definitionFit: Anisette is a sweet aniseed-flavoured liqueur, a drink taken after dinner.

clue.text: Accompanying one given cover of gun fire

indicators.note: the one is covered by the gun, which takes its place in the word

parts.note: to go with is to accompany
I is the Roman numeral for one
a firearm is an arm

explanation.surface: A soldier accompanying another is given covering fire with a gun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cover' and 'fire' together paint a military scene; fire is really ardour.
explanation.definitionFit: Fire as in passion or ardour of feeling is a synonym for heartfelt fervour and enthusiasm.

clue.text: Anne, unkindly to King ordered anthem deferrals

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are ordered anew, put into a new arrangement

parts.note: the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A monarch postpones the national anthem.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry VIII is said to have dismissed his fourth wife, Anne of Cleves, by this name after their first meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: Anne of Cleves came from near Flanders and the derisive nickname, a slur on her looks, is attributed to Henry VIII.

clue.text: Financial programme that will never take off

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Economic and Monetary Union, the EU plan for a single currency
second meaning: the big Australian bird that cannot fly

explanation.walkthrough: The surface sneers that a financial scheme is doomed; the second half literally means a bird that never gets airborne.
explanation.definitionFit: The EU's monetary union plan has this acronym, and the large flightless bird cannot leave the ground.

clue.text: Train network operator collecting money for Shylock?

indicators.note: the operator collects the coin, taking it inside

parts.note: EE is a British mobile phone network operator
Shylock, the moneylender in The Merchant of Venice, counts his ducats, gold coins

explanation.surface: A railway operator takes Venetian cash for a train fare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Train' and 'network operator' paint a railway; train is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To teach or school someone in a skill is to instruct them, a synonym of the verb in the clue.

clue.text: See 1
Char's at it busily filling rear flap

indicators.note: the reworked letters fill the char, going in its middle

parts.note: char is charred material, charcoal, so coal

indicators.note: busily working at it shakes the letters into a new order

parts.note: the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A cleaning lady works busily, stitching a coat's back flap.
explanation.walkthrough: A char is a British cleaning lady; here char means charred fuel instead.
explanation.definitionFit: The tail of a tailcoat is the long split section hanging at the back, a flap behind the wearer.

clue.text: Area parking hard, restricted by tar surface

indicators.note: the parking and hard letters are restricted, hemmed in, by the sailor

parts.note: a tar and a salt are both old words for a sailor

explanation.surface: Parking an area hard-standing, limited by tar for the surface.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tar' looks like part of the road surface; it is a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: Asphalt is the bituminous material used to pave roads and playgrounds, laid as a surface.

clue.text: Intimate cycling around part of 2?

indicators.note: the first letter cycles round to the end of the word

parts.note: an intimate is a close friend, a pal

explanation.surface: A close friend cycles round part of a mountain range.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer to 2 down is a group of mountains, so a single peak is part of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A single high peak, especially one in Switzerland, is one mountain of a larger range.

clue.text: Whom mum picked up heartlessly via old dance card?

indicators.note: the dance and old are reached via the father, who goes between them

parts.note: a ball is a formal dance

indicators.note: the father loses his heart, the central letter

parts.note: the man mum picked up is dad

explanation.surface: Who did mother pick up through an old dance card?
explanation.walkthrough: A dance card listed a woman's partners at a ball; card here is an eccentric person.
explanation.definitionFit: A card is a colourful, eccentric character, and an oddball is just such a peculiar person.

clue.text: Formal earlier dedicated work by Liberal leader should do this

parts.note: set means fixed or formal, as in a set speech
ago means in the past, earlier
an ode is a poem often dedicated to someone
x means by, as in multiplied by or 3 x 4 dimensions
liberal means generous or plentiful, ample

explanation.surface: A formal, long-standing dedication by the Liberal leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Liberal leader' looks like a party chief, but leader starts the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Anyone in charge is expected to behave as a model for followers to imitate.

clue.text: Silver, prior to marriage, kept in regularly empty drawer!

indicators.note: the silver and marriage letters are kept in the regularly picked letters
taking every other letter of empty regularly, the second and fourth

parts.note: the word whose even letters are taken
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
né, like née, means born, and introduces a name held before marriage

explanation.surface: Silver, a wedding gift, kept in an otherwise empty drawer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawer' looks like furniture, but it is something that draws, attracts.
explanation.definitionFit: A magnet draws iron towards itself, so it is fairly called something that pulls or attracts.

clue.text: See 7
Things being so easy with fish all skinned

indicators.note: each of the three words is skinned, losing its first and last letters

parts.note: the first word skinned
the second word skinned
the third word skinned

explanation.surface: A fisherman finds skinning every fish easy, things being so.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means in the present state, unchanged, exactly the circumstances as they stand.

clue.text: Run services for lip-readers fairly

indicators.note: lips form the same shapes for both phrases, so they look identical to a lip-reader, a twist on sounding alike

parts.note: a bye is a run scored in cricket without the batter hitting the ball, and rites are religious services

explanation.surface: Someone runs signed services for deaf people who lip-read.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a bye is a run taken when the ball passes the batter and the keeper untouched.
explanation.definitionFit: By rights means properly or justly, if things were done as they fairly should be.

clue.text: A 16-hour girl?

parts.note: a means one, the Roman numeral I
sixteen hours is two-thirds of a day, so two of its three letters

explanation.surface: A girl who works sixteen-hour shifts.
explanation.walkthrough: '16' looks like a cross-reference to 16 down, but it is just a number of hours.
explanation.definitionFit: Ida is a woman's given name, so the answer is simply one example of a girl.

clue.text: Suggestion hasn't left work for tattooist

indicators.note: the word lacks the letter for left, L dropped

parts.note: an inkling is a hint or slight suggestion

explanation.surface: A hint has not left work for a tattoo artist.
explanation.definitionFit: A tattooist puts ink into the skin, so applying dye with needles is their job.

clue.text: I hear setter intermittently away on cruise?

indicators.note: being away on a ship puts the letters inside the vessel

parts.note: a liner is a cruise ship

indicators.note: only the odd letters of setter are taken, on and off

parts.note: the word whose odd letters are taken

explanation.surface: A setter overhears things on and off while away on a cruise.
explanation.walkthrough: The Listener is also a famously hard crossword, so the setter fits the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Whoever says 'I hear' is one who attends with the ears, a hearer.
